translationRepairs: Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Pichang and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.
Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Picheng and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.
s0048 names Taizong's hall 丕承; 承 is chéng, so Picheng is correct and Pichang misreads 承 as 昌.
Thereupon Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Pichang and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.
Thereupon Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Picheng and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.
The literal likewise romanizes 丕承 as Pichang; Picheng matches the Chinese characters.

Chief invokers and palace attendants bore Emperor Taizong's portrait; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall. When the rites were complete, it was installed in turn at Pichang Hall with the same ceremonies as above.

Chief invokers and palace attendants bore Emperor Taizong's portrait; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall. When the rites were complete, it was installed in turn at Picheng Hall with the same ceremonies as above.
s0071 installs the portrait 於丕承殿; the hall is Picheng Hall, not Pichang Hall.

Chief invokers and palace attendants bore the imperial portrait of Emperor Taizong; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall; when the rites were complete, it was reverently installed in turn at Pichang Hall, the rites all as above.

Chief invokers and palace attendants bore the imperial portrait of Emperor Taizong; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall; when the rites were complete, it was reverently installed in turn at Picheng Hall, the rites all as above.
Literal of s0071 repeats Pichang for 丕承殿; Picheng is the accurate romanization.
Minister of War Rang served as Minister of Education; Chief Judge Tiansi of the Court of Judicial Review was dispatched to serve as Minister of Rites and act as the secondary presenter.
Minister of War Rang served as Minister of Education; Chief Judge Tianxi of the Court of Judicial Review was dispatched to serve as Minister of Rites and act as the secondary presenter.
s0165 names 大理卿天錫; 錫 is xī, so Tianxi is correct and Tiansi misreads 錫.
Minister of War Rang served as Minister of Education; the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Tiansi, was dispatched to serve as Minister of Rites and act as the secondary presenter.
Minister of War Rang served as Minister of Education; the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Tianxi, was dispatched to serve as Minister of Rites and act as the secondary presenter.
The literal also gives Tiansi for 天錫; Tianxi restores the proper reading of 錫.
s0243 is 宣孝太子廟; 宣 is xuān, so Xuanxiao is correct and Xiaoxiao drops the first character's reading.
Literal of the same heading must romanize 宣孝 as Xuanxiao, not Xiaoxiao.

The inscribing officer took the kneeling mat and inscribed the posthumous title on the back: "Spirit tablet of Crown Prince Xiaoxiao," in ink, using a glossy-lacquer mold. When finished, he handed it to the officer bearing the spirit tablet, who received it in a case covered with plum-red silk over plain silk, placed it in the casket at the seat, lowered curtains and canopies, and posted guards according to prescribed form.

The inscribing officer took the kneeling mat and inscribed the posthumous title on the back: "Spirit tablet of Crown Prince Xuanxiao," in ink, using a glossy-lacquer mold. When finished, he handed it to the officer bearing the spirit tablet, who received it in a case covered with plum-red silk over plain silk, placed it in the casket at the seat, lowered curtains and canopies, and posted guards according to prescribed form.
The inscribed title is 「宣孝太子神主」; English Xiaoxiao misromanizes 宣孝, and Xuanxiao restores it.

The inscribing officer took the kneeling mat and inscribed the posthumous title on the back: "Spirit tablet of Crown Prince Xuanxiao," in ink, using a glossy-lacquer mold; when finished, he handed it to the officer bearing the spirit tablet, who received it in a case, covered it with a plum-red silk cloth laid on a plain silk cloth, went to the seat and placed it in the casket, then lowered curtains and canopies; guards followed the prescribed form.
Literal inscription wording likewise needs Xuanxiao for 宣孝, matching the Chinese tablet text.
